RECIPROCAL STRATEGIC EQUITY SIDE LETTER

EDNA, Inc. and Pulse Intelligence Labs, Inc.

This Reciprocal Strategic Equity Side Letter (this “Side Letter”) is dated September 23, 2026 and is entered into upon execution by both Parties by and between EDNA, Inc. (“EDNA”), and Pulse Intelligence Labs, Inc., a Delaware corporation (“Pulse Intelligence Labs”).

EDNA and Pulse Intelligence Labs may each be referred to as a “Party” and collectively as the “Parties.”

The Parties are entering into that certain Strategic Partnership and Integration Agreement dated as of September 11, 2026 (the “Partnership Agreement”) and desire to reflect a deeper strategic relationship through reciprocal company-to-company equity participation, aligned long-term economic interests, and limited reciprocal participation rights in future financings.

The Parties intend this Side Letter to supplement, but not alter, the operational independence, data boundaries, Intellectual Property ownership, commercial economics, regulatory responsibilities, or allocation of responsibility established in the Partnership Agreement.

Capitalized terms not defined in this Side Letter have the meanings given in the Partnership Agreement, including Affiliate, Financing Party, Financial Distress Event, and Material Competitor.

1. RECIPROCAL STRATEGIC EQUITY COMMITMENT

Subject to:

approval by the issuing Party’s board of directors;

any required stockholder or investor approval or consent;

compliance with applicable federal and state securities laws;

compliance with the issuing Party’s certificate of incorporation, bylaws, stockholder agreements, investor-rights agreements, financing instruments, and other governing documents; and

execution of definitive warrant or other equity documentation,

Each Party shall grant to the other Party two separate rights in its common stock: (i) a Strategic Share Award covering a maximum of 200,000 shares, issued as vested without a cash purchase requirement; and (ii) a separate Strategic Partnership Warrant to purchase a maximum of 200,000 additional shares at the applicable approved exercise price. Each component vests separately over forty-eight (48) months, with 50,000 shares vesting on the first anniversary of September 11, 2026 and the remaining 150,000 shares vesting monthly over the following thirty-six (36) months, subject to the Side Letter and applicable warrant. The combined maximum is 400,000 shares per issuing Party, subject only to the proportionate corporate adjustments expressly permitted by those documents. These fixed share counts do not promise equal ownership percentages or equal dollar values in the two companies.

The Share Award and Warrant are distinct, fixed-count grants. Each covers 200,000 common shares, and neither is calculated as a percentage of Fully Diluted Capitalization. Shares delivered under one component do not reduce or satisfy the other component. Securities separately purchased in a later financing under Section 6 are outside these two grants and do not enlarge either grant’s cap.

The reciprocal equity rights are intended solely as company-to-company strategic ownership interests.

No equity or economic interest is granted under this Side Letter personally to any founder, officer, director, employee, advisor, contractor, shareholder, or other individual associated with either Party.

The PIL Strategic Vesting Share Agreement dated September 23, 2026 is the definitive instrument for PIL’s Share Award. EDNA shall deliver its corresponding definitive Strategic Share Award agreement at the coordinated closing. This Side Letter governs the shared reciprocal terms and is incorporated in those instruments. The separate PIL-to-EDNA and EDNA-to-PIL Strategic Partnership Warrants govern the additional purchase rights. The board consents authorize both components; they do not substitute a warrant for the Share Award.

Each component is denominated in the issuing Party’s common stock. Any substitution of another security class, conversion of the Share Award into a purchase right, or change to either fixed share count requires a written amendment signed by both Parties and all required corporate approvals, except for proportionate adjustments expressly permitted herein.

2. PURPOSE OF THE STRATEGIC EQUITY

The reciprocal equity rights are being established in recognition of the Parties’ anticipated contributions to the long-term strategic relationship, which may include:

Joint Services commercialization;

product and technical integration;

Clinical Handoff infrastructure;

customer and institutional development;

pilot collaboration;

joint implementation activities;

strategic market positioning;

operational coordination; and

creation of long-term enterprise value arising from the collaboration.

The equity rights do not modify the revenue-sharing provisions of the Partnership Agreement and shall not constitute payment for a specific customer contract, referral, sales transaction, Clinical Handoff, Grant payment, or other individual transaction.

Each Party shall remain responsible for its own business operations, personnel, systems, products, services, costs, and liabilities as provided in the Partnership Agreement.

3. COMMERCIAL PARTNERSHIP ISSUANCE; SECURITIES-LAW TREATMENT

The Parties intend the reciprocal equity rights to be issued as part of their strategic commercial relationship and not as consideration for the contribution of investment capital by either Party.

The Parties acknowledge, however, that the characterization and treatment of any equity issuance under applicable securities laws, existing investor agreements, financing instruments, preemptive rights, most-favored-nation provisions, rights of first offer, or similar contractual provisions shall be determined by the actual terms of those laws and agreements.

Accordingly, nothing in this Side Letter shall be interpreted as conclusively determining that a reciprocal equity issuance:

is or is not a financing transaction for all legal purposes;

is exempt from an existing investor consent requirement;

cannot trigger a contractual preemptive right, right of first offer, most-favored-nation provision, conversion provision, or similar right; or

is exempt from any securities-law filing, exemption, notice, or disclosure requirement.

Each issuing Party shall be responsible for confirming with its own counsel that its issuance complies with applicable law and existing contractual obligations before issuing the applicable warrant or equity instrument.

4. VESTING

4.1 Vesting Schedule

Subject to the conditions below, the Strategic Share Award and the Warrant of each Party shall each vest separately over forty-eight (48) months, commencing September 11, 2026, as follows:

twenty-five percent (25%), equal to 50,000 shares under each component, shall vest on September 11, 2027, the first anniversary of the Vesting Commencement Date; and

the remaining seventy-five percent (75%), equal to 150,000 shares under each component, shall vest in monthly installments during months thirteen (13) through forty-eight (48), with final vesting on September 11, 2030, subject to whole-share rounding below.

For each 200,000-share component separately, no shares vest before September 11, 2027; 50,000 vest on that date. On each monthly anniversary thereafter through September 11, 2030, the cumulative vested total is 50,000 plus the whole number obtained by rounding down 150,000 multiplied by the number of completed monthly installments after the cliff divided by 36. Each installment equals the increase in that cumulative total. The final installment vests the entire remaining balance so that the cumulative total is exactly 200,000 shares. Except for express acceleration, no partial month is credited. Proportionate stock-split and similar adjustments apply consistently to the totals and installments.

4.1A Share Award Issuance and Consideration

At the coordinated closing and subject to the closing conditions in Sections 13 and 18, each Party grants the other a contractual Strategic Share Award for 200,000 common shares. No unvested Share Award shares are issued at closing. As each installment vests, the issuing Party shall issue that vested installment without an exercise notice, cash purchase price, or election to exercise. The issuing Party shall promptly record the recipient as owner of those shares in its stock ledger and provide an electronic or certificated record. An administrative delay does not postpone vesting or cancel an accrued right to issuance.

The consideration for Share Award shares is the recipient Party’s strategic undertakings and contributions under the Partnership Agreement and this Side Letter, as authorized and valued by the issuing Party’s Board under applicable law. The Board must determine that the non-cash consideration is legally sufficient, including any applicable par-value requirement. This award does not discharge commercial payments otherwise owed. Neither Party is required to pay cash to receive vested Share Award shares.

Until Share Award shares are actually issued, the recipient holds a contractual issuance right and has no voting, dividend, or other stockholder rights solely by reason of that unissued award. Once issued, shares carry the rights of the issuing Party’s common stock, subject to lawful governing-document and transfer restrictions. Nothing herein eliminates nonwaivable statutory rights. Unvested award rights terminate as expressly provided in Section 4; issued or vested award shares are not automatically forfeited by ordinary termination.

4.1B Separate Warrant Exercise

Warrant vesting makes the vested portion eligible for purchase; it does not itself issue shares. The Holder may exercise vested purchase rights under its Warrant by delivering the required notice and paying the approved exercise price, unless an expressly permitted cashless-exercise provision applies. No early exercise of unvested rights is permitted. The Warrant has a ten-year term from its Issue Date, subject to its express earlier-termination provisions; vesting does not create a new ten-year term for each installment. The Share Award is not subject to that exercise deadline.

4.1C Proportionate Corporate Adjustments

Stock splits, reverse splits, stock dividends, recapitalizations, combinations, reclassifications, and similar changes shall result in proportionate adjustments to outstanding unissued Share Award shares and Warrant shares, preserving the intended rights without an economic windfall. Ordinary financing dilution and conversion of existing instruments do not increase either fixed-count grant. The Warrant separately governs its exercise-price adjustments.

4.2 Conditions to Continued Vesting

Continued vesting is conditioned upon:

the Partnership Agreement remaining in effect;

the recipient Party not being in an uncured material breach of the Partnership Agreement or this Side Letter;

the recipient Party continuing to materially participate in the strategic relationship in good faith; and

the recipient Party not having engaged in an Uncurable Strategic Breach as defined below.

A temporary cure period relating to an alleged curable breach shall not automatically stop vesting unless the breach remains uncured after expiration of the applicable cure period or the Parties otherwise agree in writing.

4.3 Termination Without Breach

If the Partnership Agreement expires, is not renewed, or is terminated pursuant to a contractual off-ramp or termination right without an uncured material breach by the recipient Party:

all Share Award shares vested through the effective termination date shall remain vested and, if not yet issued, shall be issued; all vested Warrant rights shall remain exercisable subject to the applicable Warrant; and

all unvested equity shall automatically terminate as of the effective termination date.

Termination of the Partnership Agreement shall not itself cause forfeiture of equity that was properly vested before termination except as expressly provided in the definitive instrument for fraud or other legally enforceable forfeiture events.

4.4 Termination Following Material Breach

If the Partnership Agreement is terminated because of a recipient Party’s uncured material breach, vesting shall cease as of the effective termination date and all then-unvested equity shall automatically terminate.

Share Award shares already issued or vested remain issued or issuable following an ordinary material breach; vested Warrant rights remain governed by the Warrant and applicable law. No provision treats Share Award shares as requiring exercise or payment.

4.5 Uncurable Strategic Breach

For purposes of this Side Letter, “Uncurable Strategic Breach” means conduct by the recipient Party that results in immediate termination rights under the Partnership Agreement and involves:

intentional and material misuse of the issuing Party’s data;

intentional unauthorized access to restricted clinical, proprietary, or Confidential Information;

verified intentional circumvention of a specifically documented Shared Account opportunity or scope, as defined in the Partnership Agreement;

fraud;

willful theft or misappropriation of the issuing Party’s Intellectual Property;

willful misconduct causing material harm to the issuing Party; or

another comparable intentional act expressly designated by the Partnership Agreement as an uncurable material breach.

Upon an Uncurable Strategic Breach:

all unvested reciprocal equity shall immediately terminate; and

any remedy affecting vested securities shall apply only to the extent expressly stated in the definitive instrument and permitted by applicable law.

Nothing in this Section creates an automatic forfeiture of legally vested securities absent an enforceable contractual basis for such forfeiture.

4.6 Repurchase of PIL Share Award Shares

The Parties expressly approve the option in Section 3.5 of the PIL Strategic Vesting Share Agreement to repurchase shares issued under that Share Award, including vested shares, at their documented original acquisition cost following the specified fraud, intellectual-property theft, misconduct or uncured material breach. Its notice, cure, final-determination, price, exercise and legal-limit provisions control. This provision expressly qualifies preservation of vested Share Award shares elsewhere in this Side Letter. It does not create an automatic forfeiture or extend that option to Warrant shares. The reciprocal award shall contain matching substantive protections, or any difference must be expressly agreed by both Parties in writing with required approvals before closing.

5. CHANGE OF CONTROL

5.1 Notice

To the extent legally and contractually permitted, a Party undergoing a proposed Change of Control shall provide the other Party reasonable notice sufficient to permit determination of the treatment of the outstanding reciprocal equity instrument.

5.2 Acceleration

Upon a Change of Control of an issuing Party occurring while the Partnership Agreement remains in effect and while the recipient Party is not in an uncured material breach:

fifty percent (50%) of the then-unvested reciprocal equity shall accelerate and vest immediately before consummation of the Change of Control.

The remaining unvested portion shall accelerate only if, in connection with or within twelve (12) months following the Change of Control:

the acquiring entity terminates the Partnership Agreement other than for material breach by the recipient Party;

the acquiring entity materially eliminates the strategic relationship;

the acquiring entity refuses to assume or honor the applicable reciprocal equity instrument; or

the acquiring entity is a material competitor of the recipient Party and the recipient Party exercises a Change-of-Control termination or exclusivity right under Section 14.4A of the Partnership Agreement.

Upon one of those events, one hundred percent (100%) of the remaining unvested equity shall accelerate.

The acceleration provisions apply separately to the unvested Share Award and the unvested Warrant. Accelerated Share Award shares shall be issued in time to receive the applicable transaction consideration, or the acquirer shall provide economically equivalent treatment if issuance is not practicable. Warrant assumption, exercise, cashless exercise, and economically equivalent treatment are governed by the applicable Warrant. Acceleration does not enlarge either component’s maximum share count.

5.3 No Acceleration for Recipient Breach

No unvested equity shall accelerate in favor of a recipient Party that, at the time of the Change of Control, is in an uncured material breach or has committed an Uncurable Strategic Breach.

6. FINANCING PARTICIPATION RIGHT

6.1 Notice of Qualified Financing

At the commencement of a Qualified Financing, the issuing Party shall, subject to applicable confidentiality restrictions and legal obligations, provide the other Party reasonable written notice containing available material information regarding:

security type;

price;

material economic terms;

expected closing timeline; and

subscription process.

The issuing Party shall not be required to disclose another investor’s confidential information or information it is legally prohibited from disclosing.

6.2 Participation Right

The receiving Party shall have the right, but not the obligation, to purchase securities in the Qualified Financing on substantially the same economic terms and at the same price applicable to similarly situated new investors, subject to:

applicable securities-law requirements;

required investor qualifications;

board approval;

allocation limitations imposed by the financing;

rights previously granted to existing investors; and

execution of the applicable financing documents.

Unless otherwise approved by the issuing Party’s board, the receiving Party’s participation right shall be limited to the amount reasonably necessary to maintain its then-current percentage ownership immediately following the financing.

6.3 No Anti-Dilution Guarantee

The financing participation right constitutes an opportunity to invest additional capital and does not constitute an anti-dilution or non-dilution guarantee.

If the receiving Party declines to participate, is legally unable to participate, fails to timely participate, or is subject to allocation limitations applicable to the financing, its percentage ownership may be diluted in the same manner as other similarly situated equity holders.

No Party is guaranteed any fixed or perpetual ownership percentage. The two 200,000-share components are fixed share counts, subject only to their express proportionate corporate adjustments.

6.4 Election Period

The receiving Party shall have ten (10) business days following receipt of financing documentation reasonably sufficient to evaluate the opportunity to elect whether to participate, unless:

a shorter response period is reasonably required by the financing timeline and is agreed in writing; or

the issuing Party grants a longer period.

The participation right shall not block, delay, condition, or otherwise impair the issuing Party’s ability to complete a financing.

6.5 Termination of Participation Right

Unless otherwise provided in the definitive warrant, the financing participation right shall terminate upon the earliest of:

termination of the Partnership Agreement;

a Change of Control of the issuing Party;

the recipient Party committing an Uncurable Strategic Breach; or

such other date as mutually agreed in writing.

Termination of the participation right shall not affect equity already vested or securities previously purchased.

6.6 Independent Financing and Investor Non-Interference

Each Party may raise capital independently and on different valuations, amounts, security types, timelines, and investor terms. Neither Party is required to match the other Party’s financing, use the same SPV or investment vehicle, accept the same investors, or maintain equivalent capitalization.

The financing participation right in this Side Letter is a limited opportunity to invest; it is not a veto right over the issuing Party’s financing and does not permit the receiving Party to block a larger or company-specific investment in the issuing Party.

No financing by either Party shall, by itself, create any ownership, governance, approval, information, lien, or economic right in the other Party. Neither Party shall knowingly grant a Financing Party a contractual right to compel circumvention of the Partnership Agreement, obtain the other Party’s protected data or Intellectual Property, or require the other Party to accept financing, transfer assets, change capitalization, or waive rights.

If a Material Competitor of the other Party receives a board seat, observer right, or enhanced information right in the issuing Party, the issuing Party shall maintain commercially reasonable confidentiality and information-firewall protections consistent with the Partnership Agreement. Nothing in this paragraph gives the other Party a general approval right over investors.

7. NO CROSS-COMPANY LIABILITY OR CAPITAL OBLIGATION

Neither Party shall be required by reason of the reciprocal equity arrangement to:

contribute capital to the other Party;

guarantee the other Party’s obligations;

participate in a future financing;

fund operating losses;

guarantee customer contracts;

assume debt;

fund litigation;

contribute to a Grant;

fund product-development costs; or

provide additional financial support.

Each Party’s financial obligations shall be limited to those expressly stated in the Partnership Agreement, this Side Letter, the definitive equity instrument, or another separately signed agreement.

8. NO RIGHTS TO THE OTHER PARTY’S INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY OR DATA

Equity ownership under this Side Letter shall not provide either Party with any right, license, ownership interest, access right, inspection right, or other entitlement to the other Party’s:

Intellectual Property;

source code;

algorithms;

AI models;

model weights;

prompts;

datasets;

clinical information;

performance information;

customer information;

Confidential Information;

data architecture;

clinical workflows; or

proprietary business information,

except as separately provided in the Partnership Agreement or another signed agreement.

The issuance of equity shall not alter the system, data, or Intellectual Property boundaries established in the Partnership Agreement and Exhibits A and B.

9. NO CONTROL, GOVERNANCE, OR FIDUCIARY RIGHTS

Except for rights necessarily arising from the actual class of securities issued and rights expressly provided in definitive documents, the reciprocal strategic equity arrangement shall not create:

a board seat;

board observer right;

management authority;

veto right;

approval right over ordinary business operations;

control over product development;

control over clinical operations;

control over financing;

fiduciary relationship;

agency relationship;

legal partnership; or

joint venture.

Neither Party may represent that it controls, owns, operates, or manages the other Party merely because it holds securities issued pursuant to this Side Letter.

9A. NO INVESTOR, LENDER, OR CREDITOR CONTROL OVER THE OTHER PARTY

No investor, lender, creditor, Financing Party, board designee, board observer, Affiliate, or other third party of one Party acquires any authority through the reciprocal equity arrangement to bind, manage, control, direct, inspect, or obtain protected information from the other Party.

No Party may pledge, encumber, or grant a security interest in the other Party’s strategic equity, data, Intellectual Property, customer rights, Grant proceeds, or assets except to the extent the issuing Party separately consents in writing and applicable law and governing documents permit. For clarity, a Party may finance and encumber its own assets and issued securities subject to applicable restrictions.

10. TRANSFER RESTRICTIONS

The reciprocal strategic equity rights and securities issued pursuant to them shall be subject to:

applicable federal and state securities laws;

the issuing Party’s governing documents;

applicable transfer restrictions;

any right of first refusal or similar rights validly applicable to the security;

restrictive legends; and

the terms of the definitive warrant or equity instrument.

Unless otherwise approved by the issuing Party’s board, neither Party may transfer unissued Share Award rights or an unexercised reciprocal strategic warrant to:

a direct material competitor of the issuing Party;

an entity acquiring the recipient Party primarily for purposes of obtaining the strategic warrant; or

another third party where the transfer would reasonably be expected to create material competitive, regulatory, data-security, or governance risk to the issuing Party.

Any permitted transferee shall take the instrument subject to applicable restrictions.

If an unissued Share Award right or unexercised Warrant is transferred to an approved Affiliate and that transferee later ceases to be an Affiliate of the original recipient, the transferee shall, to the extent legally permitted, transfer the right back to the original recipient or another approved Affiliate unless the issuing Party’s board approves continued ownership in writing. No Affiliate transfer may be used to evade a competitor-transfer restriction.

10A. FINANCIAL DISTRESS; NO CROSS-DEFAULT

A Financial Distress Event affecting one Party does not create a default by the other Party, require the other Party to contribute capital, accelerate the other Party’s equity obligations, or create creditor rights in the other Party.

Treatment of vested and unvested strategic equity during a Financial Distress Event shall continue to be governed by this Side Letter, the applicable Warrant, the Partnership Agreement, governing documents, and applicable law. No provision shall be interpreted to create an automatic termination or forfeiture solely because of bankruptcy or insolvency where such treatment is unenforceable under applicable law.

Any creditor, receiver, trustee, assignee, or successor taking rights in a Party or its property takes no greater rights in the other Party’s data, Intellectual Property, customer relationships, or independent operations than the affected Party itself possessed under the Partnership Agreement.

11. NO EFFECT ON COMMERCIAL ECONOMICS

The reciprocal equity rights are separate from the revenue-sharing and commercial economics established in the Partnership Agreement.

Neither Party may:

reduce the other Party’s contractual revenue share because it holds reciprocal equity;

treat the equity as payment for services otherwise payable under the Partnership Agreement;

offset amounts owed under Joint Services against the value of the reciprocal equity;

use the equity to alter Shared Account economics; or

characterize the reciprocal equity as creating ownership of Joint Services revenue.

Equity participation and commercial revenue sharing constitute separate economic arrangements.

12. DEFINITIONS

“Change of Control”

“Change of Control” means:

a merger, consolidation, or similar business combination following which the persons owning a majority of the issuing Party’s voting power immediately before the transaction no longer own a majority of the voting power of the surviving entity;

a sale or transfer of more than fifty percent (50%) of the issuing Party’s voting power;

a sale of all or substantially all of the issuing Party’s assets; or

another transaction having substantially similar economic effect.

A bona fide equity financing primarily intended to raise capital shall not constitute a Change of Control merely because new investors acquire significant equity, unless the transaction otherwise satisfies this definition.

“Fully Diluted Capitalization”

“Fully Diluted Capitalization” means the issuing Party’s outstanding capital stock or equivalent equity interests calculated on an as-converted and as-exercised basis, including, to the extent determined applicable by the issuing Party and its counsel:

outstanding common stock;

preferred stock on an as-converted basis;

outstanding options;

warrants;

convertible securities;

SAFEs or similar convertible instruments;

reserved but unissued shares under an equity incentive plan; and

other outstanding rights to acquire equity.

The capitalization calculation shall be certified or approved in good faith by the issuing Party’s board of directors.

“Qualified Financing”

“Qualified Financing” means a bona fide equity or equity-linked financing undertaken primarily to raise capital from one or more third-party investors.

Qualified Financing does not include, unless the Parties expressly agree otherwise:

grants;

NSF or other governmental awards;

customer contracts;

commercial revenue;

ordinary-course commercial loans;

equipment financing;

venture debt without a material equity component;

commercial strategic warrants similar to those contemplated by this Side Letter;

employee or advisor equity issuances;

ordinary equity-plan grants;

exercises of previously outstanding securities; or

strategic commercial transactions not primarily undertaken to raise investment capital.

“Vesting Commencement Date”

“Vesting Commencement Date” means September 11, 2026 for both the Share Award and the Warrant of each issuing Party. No award becomes effective, no shares are issued, and no purchase right is exercisable before the coordinated closing conditions are satisfied. Any elapsed service credited from that commencement date remains subject to the vesting conditions; actual execution dates shall be recorded accurately.

13. CONDITIONS, APPROVALS, AND SECURITIES COMPLIANCE

Each issuance is conditioned upon:

approval of the issuing Party’s board of directors;

any legally or contractually required stockholder or investor approval;

determination of an available exemption from registration or other lawful issuance pathway;

completion of required federal or state filings or notices;

compliance with applicable corporate law;

compliance with existing financing and investor agreements; and

execution of definitive equity documentation acceptable to the issuing Party and its counsel.

Each Party acknowledges that securities issued by a privately held company may constitute restricted securities and may not be freely transferable or resold except pursuant to registration or an available exemption from registration and subject to applicable contractual restrictions.

Each Party shall be responsible for its own legal, tax, accounting, and securities-law advice concerning receipt, issuance, exercise, ownership, and disposition of the reciprocal equity rights.

14. RELATIONSHIP TO PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT

This Side Letter supplements the Partnership Agreement.

Except with respect to the reciprocal equity rights expressly described herein, nothing in this Side Letter modifies:

Joint Services economics;

Independent Contract rights;

Shared Account protections;

exclusivity;

non-circumvention;

Intellectual Property ownership;

Data Privacy obligations;

Clinical Handoff boundaries;

allocation of operational responsibility;

indemnification;

limitation of liability;

termination rights; or

dispute-resolution rights

under the Partnership Agreement.

If there is a conflict:

the Partnership Agreement shall control with respect to commercial, operational, data, clinical, Intellectual Property, and partnership matters; and

this Side Letter shall control the separate Strategic Share Awards, fixed counts, and shared vesting and reciprocity terms; each Warrant shall control only its purchase mechanics, including its approved exercise price, exercise period, notices, and treatment on exercise. Neither Warrant reduces or replaces the separate Share Award.

No definitive warrant may materially alter the reciprocal economic intent of this Side Letter unless separately approved in writing by both Parties.

15. RECIPROCITY

The Parties intend the economic and legal protections of this Side Letter to operate reciprocally.

Neither Party shall be entitled to materially more favorable vesting, acceleration, financing participation, transfer, forfeiture, or Change-of-Control treatment than the other Party solely by virtue of differences in the drafting of its definitive warrant.

The same fixed share counts and vesting schedules apply reciprocally even though the companies’ share values and ownership percentages may differ. Legally necessary procedural differences shall not alter the fixed counts, separate components, or agreed substantive protections without both Parties’ written approval.

16. AMENDMENTS

No amendment, waiver, or modification of this Side Letter shall be effective unless made in writing and signed by authorized representatives of both Parties.

17. COUNTERPARTS AND ELECTRONIC SIGNATURES

This Side Letter may be executed in counterparts, each of which shall constitute an original and all of which together shall constitute one instrument.

Electronic signatures and electronically transmitted counterparts shall have the same force and effect as original signatures to the extent permitted by applicable law.

18. ADDITIONAL STRATEGIC EQUITY PROTECTIONS

18.1 Shared Account Precision for Equity Remedies

For purposes of any equity vesting suspension, termination, forfeiture, or other remedy based upon circumvention of a Shared Account, a “Shared Account” must be identifiable by the specific customer or counterparty, applicable department, business unit, team, purchasing entity or other defined organizational unit, and the documented commercial opportunity or scope. A relationship with a parent institution or affiliated organization alone shall not cause every present or future opportunity involving that institution or affiliate to constitute a Shared Account.

No Party shall lose unvested strategic equity based solely upon a good-faith dispute regarding opportunity attribution. An Uncurable Strategic Breach based on Shared Account circumvention requires verified intentional circumvention of a documented Shared Account opportunity or scope.

18.2 Representative Misconduct; No Automatic Cross-Default

Unauthorized misconduct by an employee, consultant, fundraiser, salesperson, advisor, or other representative shall not automatically constitute an Uncurable Strategic Breach by the appointing Party unless the conduct was authorized, directed, knowingly ratified, or materially enabled by that Party, or the Party fails to take commercially reasonable corrective action after receiving notice. Each Party remains responsible for conduct legally attributable to it and shall promptly investigate, stop, and remediate known unauthorized conduct affecting the strategic relationship.

18.3 Closing Capitalization Certificate

Before either component becomes effective, the issuing Party shall deliver a board-approved capitalization and share-reservation certificate confirming: 200,000 common shares reserved for the Strategic Share Award and 200,000 additional common shares reserved for the Warrant; sufficient authorized and uncommitted shares; the approved non-cash consideration for the Share Award; the Warrant exercise price per share and aggregate exercise cost; the applicable issue and vesting dates; required corporate and investor approvals; and the treatment of outstanding stock, options, warrants, convertible notes, SAFEs, and equity-plan reserves. The certificate shall disclose the resulting ownership percentages and avoid double counting shares reallocated from a plan reserve. Capitalization or convertible-instrument calculations are disclosure and authorization matters and shall not increase or decrease either fixed 200,000-share component. Each Party shall acknowledge the other Party’s certificate before the coordinated closing. No certificate or administrative entry may substitute for an approval required by law or the governing documents.

18.3A PIL Share Reserve Reallocation

PIL’s current proposed capitalization setup separately reserves 1,600,000 common shares for its Equity Incentive Plan and 400,000 common shares for strategic awards. These amounts do not constitute proof of effective approval or available authorized shares. PIL shall complete the required Plan approvals, any necessary founder share return, and capitalization certification before closing. This Side Letter does not reduce the incentive reserve to 600,000 shares or itself return founder shares. EDNA shall separately certify its lawful source of 400,000 common shares; no total capitalization is assumed for EDNA.

18.4 Reciprocal Closing Condition

PIL’s Share Award and Warrant shall have no force or effect until EDNA delivers its valid reciprocal Share Award and separate Warrant, required approvals, and capitalization certificate at coordinated closing. EDNA’s reciprocal Share Award must represent 2.0% of EDNA’s fully diluted capitalization at that closing. If the fixed 200,000 shares do not meet that condition, both Parties must sign an amendment and obtain all required corporate approvals before closing; there is no automatic change to either share count. The condition is an initial closing test, not a continuing anti-dilution right. The PIL Share Award’s Section 6 governs reciprocal delivery and later breach remedies.

The Parties intend this Side Letter (including both Share Awards), reciprocal board approvals, capitalization and share-reservation certificates, and both purchase Warrants to close as one coordinated package. Neither Party is required to deliver effective rights materially earlier than the other Party unless expressly agreed in writing. Signing a document does not dispense with its outstanding closing conditions.

18.5 Financing, Affiliate, and Third-Party Independence

Before coordinated closing, each Party shall confirm that the reciprocal strategic equity documents do not grant the other Party or any investor, lender, SPV, Affiliate, or financing source of the other Party any direct governance right over the issuing Party beyond rights inherent in the actual securities issued and the limited rights expressly stated in these documents.

Any future subsidiary, Affiliate, SPV, or financing structure shall remain subject to the anti-evasion, data/IP, Shared Account, and financing-independence protections of the Partnership Agreement. No such structure automatically becomes a holder, beneficiary, or permitted transferee of the reciprocal strategic equity.

18.6 PROTECTED DATA AND JOINT RESEARCH RIGHTS

Strategic Share Awards, Warrants, financing participation rights, shareholder status, due-diligence activity, investor status, affiliate status, or the strategic relationship do not grant either Party any additional right to access, inspect, use, retain, research, publish, commercialize, train models upon, benchmark, or obtain the other Party’s Protected Data or Joint Research Data. Any Joint Research use must be separately authorized under the Partnership Agreement and an applicable written research protocol or Research and Publication Addendum. These restrictions are reciprocal; where EDNA Protected Clinical Data constitutes PHI, HIPAA and other applicable law provide additional protections and shall control to the extent applicable.

EXECUTION; COUNTERPARTS; ELECTRONIC SIGNATURES

Execution Date. This revised Side Letter is dated September 23, 2026 and takes effect upon authorized execution by both Parties. It replaces prior unsigned drafts. Any previously executed side letter is amended and restated only upon authorized execution of this revision by both Parties; no prior signed record is altered. Equity effectiveness remains subject to the coordinated closing conditions. The September 11, 2026 vesting commencement date remains unchanged.
